key_insight: Conditioning recurrent forecasts on temperature and thermal rate enables accurate prediction of grain size distribution evolution during non-isothermal heat treatment.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computationally efficient route to predicting heat-treatment-driven microstructure evolution without repeatedly running costly grain-growth simulations.
method: Encode grain size distributions with a convolutional neural network.
Embed instantaneous temperature and thermal rate with a dedicated multilayer perceptron.
Forecast temporal evolution with a recurrent network trained on validated front-tracking simulations.
evidence_signal: Across all simulations, k-fold cross-validation yielded mean relative errors of 2.99% for one-hour cycles and 4.51% for four-hour cycles, with R² > 0.99; ten simulations spanning four unseen thermal histories yielded errors of 1.91–14.66%.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based, and the wider error range on unseen thermal histories warrants caution when extrapolating to new processing conditions.
paper_title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
